---
title: "Environmental Chemistry"
---

How do chemical reactions determine what happens to a substance in air, water,
and soil? We connect molecular properties, equilibria, reaction rates, and
partitioning to environmental transport and exposure.

::: {.callout-note}
The first teaching draft is available for carbonate and gas chemistry.
The remaining topics are outlined for development.
:::

The proposed sequence follows atmosphere, water, and the terrestrial environment,
with particular attention to aquatic chemistry. See the
[content overview](overview.qmd) for the topics and chemical questions.

Calculations begin with a small worked example. Selected exercises then reuse
R for tables, plots, and reproducible explanations of chemical results.

Start with [carbonate and gas chemistry](carbonate-gases/notes.qmd): short
lectures, worked examples, exercises, and a species-distribution plot in R.
